outputText: ```json { "Subject": "Single seated person", "Subject_type": "Human (seated)", "Setting": "Interior studio/workspace", "Framing": "Medium close-up (slightly above waist level, centered on subject’s torso and hands)", "Lighting": "Natural + soft artificial; warm tones on the left side of face, slightly shadowed right side", "Location": "Indoor room with wooden furniture, large windows/frames on walls, neutral-toned floor", "Actors": [ { "reference": "Person A", "description": "Female seated artist", "position": "Foreground center", "orientation": "Front-facing" } ], "Remarkable_features": ["White cropped sweater with ribbed texture", "Light blue jeans rolled at ankles", "Slightly upward gaze and open-mouthed expression", "Left hand on knee, right hand pointing forward", "Green faux grass texture forming a heart shape in front"], "Animal_analogy_enabled": true, "Animal_analogy": "A person kneeling in contemplation over a carefully arranged floral/geometric pattern (similar to a bee inspecting a hive entrance).", "Continuity_person_anchors": ["White sweater with ribbed texture", "Light blue jeans and rolled cuffs", "Slightly upturned mouth, open expression", "Hand positions (left on knee, right pointing forward)", "Hair length and style"], "Continuity_location_anchors": ["Wooden floor with circular pattern of round wooden discs", "Large blank canvas or paper with faint heart/geometric designs underneath the green grass", "Green faux grass forming a heart shape on the table", "Small jars/containers with liquids on the right side of the table", "Open doorway framing in the background"], "What_stays_consistent_for_next_shot
prompt: Describe only the visible shot for continuity. Return concise labeled lines for Subject, Subject type, Setting, Framing, Lighting, Location, Actors, Description, Remarkable features, Animal analogy enabled, Animal analogy, Continuity person anchors, Continuity location anchors, and what should stay consistent for the next video shot. Subject type describes visible form only, such as single seated person, partial person, animal close-up, or no person visible. Remarkable features lists two to five concrete visible details that help distinguish this frame, including ordinary details when nothing unusual stands out; do not return none or an empty list while visible person, clothing, pose, object, color, or background details exist. Animal analogy enabled is true for the closest plausible visual analogy whenever a visible subject has a comparable posture, silhouette, or gesture; weak resemblance counts and low confidence is allowed. Set it false only when no visible form can reasonably be compared. Never invent a literal animal or infer personality, identity, ethnicity, age, profession, or biology. Continuity person anchors lists concrete visible person details useful for the next image: clothing, face, hair, pose, gaze, hands, or body position. Continuity location anchors lists concrete visible room details useful for the next image: frames, furniture, windows, lighting, colors, or background geometry. Continuity anchors are split into these two fields; do not merge person and location details. Actors must be a JSON array with one object per real visible person using keys reference, description, position, and orientation. Use position to report depth and frame placement, for example foreground left, midground center, background right, or top center. Use orientation to report front-facing, side-facing, or back-facing. If two people are visible, return two separate actor objects. Do not include people shown only in posters, artwork, screens, mirrors, or reflections.
